newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Shenzhen B shares end higher on selected buying.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares end higher on selected buying.

text.p: Shenzhen's B share index closed slightly higher on Monday on buying of a few issues with good interim results, brokers said.
Shenzhen's A share market rose on Monday due to speculative demand for third-liners, they said.
The B share index climbed 0.93 point, or 1.07 percent, to close at 88.43, but turnover shrank to HK$24.14 million from HK$62.04 million on Friday.
The A share index rose 6.21 points, or 2.38 percent, to end at 267.28, with turnover rising to 4.52 billion yuan from the previous session's 3.01 billion yuan.

Guangdong Expressway edged up HK$0.16, or 3.46 percent, to HK$4.79. Automobile parts producer Wuxi Weifu was the worst performer, sliding HK$0.46 or 14.47 percent, to HK$2.72 on thin volume of 9,900 shares.
Hainan Pearl River lost HK$0.08, or 4.49 percent, to HK$1.70 due to investor pessimism over the real estate developer's earnings for this year, brokers said.

Newcomer Changchai slipped HK$0.06 to HK$5.30 on profit-taking, brokers said, up from its recent offer price of HK$4.97 per share. Its trading volume on Monday reached 1.87 million shares, making it the most actively traded B stock.
The composite index gained 5.67 points, or 2.29 percent, to 252.74.
On the B share market, China Marine rose HK$0.27, or 4.71 percent, to HK$6.00. The Shekou-based company had reported solid profits for the first half of 1996.
Appliance maker Tsann Kuen followed with a gain of HK$0.09, or 3.95 percent, to HK$2.37.
Lizhu Pharmaceutical rallied HK$0.11, or 3.93 percent, to HK$2.91 and television maker Huafa climbed HK$0.06, or 3.70 percent, to HK$1.68.
On the A share market, chemical fibre maker Hainan Sea Rainbow became the highest gainer on speculative buying, brokers said. It surged 0.78 yuan, or 20.00 percent, to 4.68 yuan.
Kunming Department Store soared 0.88 yuan, or 17.60 percent, to 5.88 yuan, while welding materials producer Hubei Monkey King jumped 1.41 yuan, or 16.77 percent, to 9.82 yuan.

Zhonglian Construction Equipment, whose 12.50 million class A shares were listed in Shenzhen on Friday, fell 0.85 yuan, or 8.33 percent, to 9.35 yuan on Monday as investors took profits, brokers said. The A shares were issued at 4.00 yuan per share earlier this month.
